newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends up on exporter demand, rain delays.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends up on exporter demand, rain delays.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended up on exporter demand and rain delays in the harvest along with a firm CBOT soycomplex, traders said.
"Cargill's a scale-up seller of the Nov, there were Japanese sales overnight and we're up on Chicago. There's not many hedges, the rain's delaying harvest," a trader said.
Japan bought 5,000-6,000 tonnes overnight. Europe was said to have bought 60,000 tonnes since Aug 30.
November canola rose $4 to $428.30, January rose $2.60 to $432.10. Volume was 3,765.
October flax rose $3.40 to $386.40 with UGG selling to commercials houses, traders said. Volume was 37 lots.
"The rain's limiting farmer deliveries of feed grains," a trader said. Oats did not trade.
October feed wheat fell $0.20 to $208.40, Dec was up $0.50 to $193.60 on commercial buying. Alberta Wheat Pool sold the Oct-Dec at $16, traders said. Volume was 1,000.
November western barley rose $2 to $152.70 on commercials and Eastern Canadian feed lot demand, February up $1.30 to $157. Eight hundred Nov-Feb spread at $4.50. Volume was 2,200.
UGG bought peas up US$1 to US$210 in the Oct, US$211 in Dec. Oct-Dec spread at US$1. Volume was 483 lots.
(All values in Canadian dollars/tonne except peas, oats)
